newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary sees Takarekbank sale tender in Nov-Dec.
newsitem.headline: Hungary sees Takarekbank sale tender in Nov-Dec.

text.p: Hungary is likely to publish a tender for the privatisation of savings bank Takarekbank in November or December, the privatisation agency APV said on Thursday.
"The tender is not likely to be published before November, but certainly it will be this year," APV Managing Director Istvan Abel told Reuters.

Austria's GiroCredit Bank AG, Germany's Deutsche Genossenschaftsbank (DG) and the insurance group Allianz AG have all expressed interest in buying Takarekbank, which represents most of Hungary's savings cooperatives.
The three have been joined this week by the U.S. insurance holding Cuna Mutual Group (CMG), the daily Vilaggazdasag said on Thursday quoting CMG Vice-President Jacek J. Ciancara.
Ciancara was quoted as saying said CMG would like to acquire a minority stake in Takarekbank, joining the buyer of a larger stake.
He hinted that the other investor would preferably be DG Bank, but not Allianz since as an insurance company it is a direct competitor.
Abel said the winner of the tender will have to increase Takarekbank's registered capital, which amounts to 1.3 billion forints.
Zsolt Hernadi, Takarekbank's Chief Executive told Vilaggazdasag the bank needed a capital increase of 700 million to two billion forints.
